title: POC Weekly Security Sync - Valortech
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report and pen-test summary (Alex) by 2026-02-20
Valortech to provide SAML metadata and IdP test account (Ravi) by 2026-02-22
Schedule dedicated network walk-through for VPC peering and egress rules (Priya/Alex) week of 2026-02-23
Run initial audit-log retention smoke test on staging and share logs (Elena) by 2026-02-24
action_items: Alex: Attach SOC2 and security pack to CRM and email to Ravi by 2026-02-20
Priya: Set up VPC peering design call and invite Valortech network team by 2026-02-23
Ravi: Share SAML metadata + test account creds (scoped) by 2026-02-22
Elena: Run the audit log export for last 7 days and confirm retention settings by 2026-02-24
summary: Weekly POC security check-in. Covered SSO/SAML integration, audit log retention and formatting, data retention and redaction policy during pilot, SOC2 docs and timeline, KMS/HSM options, and VPC/private connectivity. Agreed on SOC2 share, SAML metadata exchange, and scheduling a network design deep dive for VPC peering. Action items assigned for next week.
topics: VPC peering and private deployment options
transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 - Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is our weekly POC security sync with Valortech. We've got Priya from SE and Jon from CSM. How's everyone doing?
00:12 Speaker 2 - Maya: Good thanks, Alex. Busy week but all set to go over the security items.
00:20 Speaker 3 - Ravi: Hi all, Ravi here, want to make sure we cover SSO and audit logs first.
00:28 Speaker 1 - Alex: Sure, let's start with SSO. Priya can you give a quick status on the SAML integration?
00:35 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yeah, we pushed the test SP metadata to the dev IdP yesterday. We saw one mismatch on NameID format - Valortech IdP expects transient, our default is persistent, so need to confirm which attribute you want for user mapping.
00:50 Speaker 3 - Ravi: We prefer transient for the pilot, we don't want long-lived identities in there. Also want assertion encryption, can Redwood support encrypted assertions?
01:00 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yes we do, we support encrypted assertions. We'll need your certificate and we can swap our metadata. We'll also provide a test account.
01:12 Speaker 2 - Maya: Quick question about groups/roles mapping - we use Azure AD groups to map to RBAC. Is there an automatic sync or do we send group claims?
01:22 Speaker 4 - Priya: We support group claims in the SAML assertion; we can map to RBAC in the console but for the POC we'd probably keep a simple mapping - one group equals admin/dev. We can demo that in the test IdP.
01:35 Speaker 5 - Jon: For audit and compliance later, we'll capture who did what in the logs, so group mappings do show up in events.
01:45 Speaker 3 - Ravi: Great. On audit logs, our requirement is 7 years for certain financial telemetry, but for the POC we only need 90 days. What do you store by default and can we export raw logs?
02:00 Speaker 4 - Priya: Out of the box we keep granular audit events for 90 days in the hosted product. For Dedicated/Private you can configure longer retention and archive to your S3 or SIEM. We can export raw logs in JSON or newline-delimited format.
02:15 Speaker 3 - Ravi: How about redaction? Some logs contain prompt inputs that may include PII; what's the POC behavior?
02:25 Speaker 1 - Alex: Good callout. For the pilot we have two options: 1) Mask or redact prompt inputs at ingestion (we can enable prompt redaction filter) or 2) Keep full logs but restrict access and export to Valortech controlled S3. Which do you prefer for initial test?
02:40 Speaker 2 - Maya: For the POC let's do redaction on prompts, and we can test full export later when we evaluate Dedicated.
02:50 Speaker 3 - Ravi: Sounds right. Also need to confirm encryption at rest and KMS usage. For our security policy keys must be customer-managed.
03:00 Speaker 4 - Priya: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. For hosted we offer service-managed keys by default and KMS bring-your-own via dedicated contracts. We can document the exact KMS flow in the security pack.
03:18 Speaker 3 - Ravi: Timeline on SOC2 docs and pen test? We asked for SOC2 Type II and recent penetration test summary.
03:25 Speaker 1 - Alex: We'll send the SOC2 Type II report and pen-test summary by Friday 2026-02-20. Note pen test reports redacted in parts for public distribution, but we can provide executive summary.
03:38 Speaker 3 - Ravi: Executive summary is fine to start. We'll follow up if we need the redacted details.
03:44 Speaker 2 - Maya: For data residency, any chance to pin logs / storage region? We want US-east for now.
03:52 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yes you can pin region in Dedicated and in hosted we can select region-based tenancy; we'll note US-east for the POC environment.
04:02 Speaker 5 - Jon: Remember the POC is on hosted but with options to move to Dedicated; we'll capture the config differences in the doc.
04:10 Speaker 3 - Ravi: For network connectivity, Valortech prefers VPC peering to avoid public egress. Does Redwood support VPC peering or private link?
04:20 Speaker 4 - Priya: We support both VPC peering and private link options depending on cloud. We should schedule a network design call with your network team, there are some egress rules and IAM roles that need to be aligned.
04:33 Speaker 6 - Samir: I can join that call. Our firewall team needs the CIDR ranges and egress ports.
04:40 Speaker 4 - Priya: We'll provide CIDRs and port list; typical ports are 443 outbound for control and optional 22 for bastion if using dedicated infra.
04:50 Speaker 3 - Ravi: Ok. On retention and deletions - if a user requests deletion under policy, can Redwood delete prompt history for that user in hosted POC?
05:00 Speaker 1 - Alex: We support deletion requests; in hosted we can delete user-level history on request and provide confirmation. For assured cryptographic deletion you'd want Dedicated or customer-managed storage. We'll document the deletion SLA for the pilot.
05:14 Speaker 2 - Maya: Also want to test audit queries - can we run queries against logs to find all accesses by a principal?
05:22 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yes, the console has an audit search UI and we can provide API access to run queries and export results. We'll enable API keys scoped for audit export.
05:34 Speaker 3 - Ravi: Please scope the API keys to read-only for logs so we don't accidentally modify configs.
05:40 Speaker 4 - Priya: Absolutely. We'll create scoped tokens for that.
05:46 Speaker 1 - Alex: Let's talk about the SAML test plan and next steps: Ravi, can you share SAML metadata and a test user by Monday?
05:55 Speaker 3 - Ravi: I'll share a metadata file and a test account limited to dev group by 2026-02-22.
06:02 Speaker 1 - Alex: Great. Priya will send config steps and we'll update the integration doc.
06:08 Speaker 4 - Priya: I'll also attach the sample mapping for group claims.
06:12 Speaker 2 - Maya: One more item — legal asked about subprocessors and data flow diagrams. Can you share a data flow and list of subprocessors?
06:22 Speaker 1 - Alex: Yes, the security pack includes a subprocessor list and a data flow diagram. We'll attach to CRM.
06:29 Speaker 3 - Ravi: For logging format, we need JSON with specific fields: timestamp, principal, event_type, model_id, truncated_prompt_hash. Is that supported?
06:40 Speaker 4 - Priya: We can include custom fields and a prompt hash field; we can export as NDJSON with those keys. We'll prototype with last 7 days.
06:50 Speaker 2 - Maya: Will the prompt hash be reversible? We want a non-reversible digest so we can match records without storing plaintext.
07:00 Speaker 4 - Priya: We'll use SHA-256 based hashing on ingest as an option so the raw prompt isn't stored. That meets non-reversible requirement for the POC.
07:12 Speaker 5 - Jon: We'll add that to the audit smoke test.
07:18 Speaker 3 - Ravi: Pen test — we need to know if Redwood runs regular internal pentesting and frequencies.
07:25 Speaker 1 - Alex: We run annual third-party pen tests and continuous internal scanning. We'll include cadence in the security doc.
07:32 Speaker 3 - Ravi: Great. If we move to Dedicated, we need a contractual clause for yearly pen tests and access to results.
07:40 Speaker 1 - Alex: Noted, legal will handle that during contract negotiations.
07:46 Speaker 2 - Maya: Any limitations on redaction? Sometimes redaction affects debugging. Can we enable structured redaction so we still get metadata but hide PII?
07:58 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yes structured redaction keeps metadata fields (tokens, lengths) but removes sensitive spans. That is our standard. We'll enable structured redaction for the POC dataset.
08:10 Speaker 6 - Samir: On the VPC peering, what's the expected SLA impact? We want to know latencies and any changes to failover model.
08:21 Speaker 4 - Priya: Peering is low-latency but adds dependency on your network. For high availability we'd recommend multi-az peering and health-check endpoints. We'll provide SLO guidance in the VPC design doc.
08:36 Speaker 3 - Ravi: For logs export frequency - can we stream logs to SIEM in near real-time?
08:45 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yes, we support streaming via Kinesis/Firehose or direct SIEM connectors; near real-time with a few seconds to a minute lag depending on throughput.
08:56 Speaker 2 - Maya: Good. On identity, do you support SCIM for provisioning users?
09:02 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yes SCIM provisioning is supported; we can enable for the POC if you want to test automated user lifecycle.
09:10 Speaker 3 - Ravi: We'll keep SCIM disabled for now and do SAML-only until initial sign-off.
09:16 Speaker 1 - Alex: OK, recap of agreed items: SOC2 pack and pen test summary by 2026-02-20, SAML metadata from Valortech by 2026-02-22, VPC design meeting week of 2026-02-23, and audit log smoke test by 2026-02-24. Anything else?
09:30 Speaker 2 - Maya: Can you also share the sample NDJSON audit schema so our SIEM folks can map fields?
09:36 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yes we'll attach the schema in the follow-up email.
09:40 Speaker 5 - Jon: I'll add items to CRM and send a calendar invite for the network design.
09:46 Speaker 3 - Ravi: One more ask: for the POC acceptance criteria, we want SSO working, logs exported to our staging SIEM, and prompt redaction enabled. If those three are satisfied we'll sign-off the security gating.
09:59 Speaker 1 - Alex: That's reasonable. We'll work to get those done.
10:05 Speaker 2 - Maya: Thanks, that's all from me.
10:08 Speaker 6 - Samir: Thanks everyone.
10:10 Speaker 1 - Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the security pack and next steps. Talk next week.
10:18 End of transcript
